evals.name: customer-invoices-endpoint
evals.prompt: The dashboard's customer page needs that customer's invoices. Add an endpoint for it: newest first, optional status filter, paged the same way as /customers.
evals.expected_output: A new route (for example GET /customers/{customer_id}/invoices) in the existing FastAPI service, following its layers: SQL only in a repository with bound parameters, database calls through the threadpool-backed Database wrapper, org scoping that answers 404 for another organisation's customer, drafts never returned and not requestable (ADR 0002), a status filter limited to open, paid and void with anything else a 422, keyset paging newest first by a stated sort key (issued_at, created_at, or issued_at falling back to created_at) with an id tie-break; inv_a1_2 and inv_a1_3 tie on both issued_at and created_at, so every choice has to page across a tie, limit bounded at 100 through the shared pagination helpers, and items in the same integer minor-unit shape as GET /invoices/{invoice_id}. The run finds that issued_at is nullable and that the seed holds a void invoice that was never issued (inv_a1_6, issued_at NULL, as ADR 0002 allows), and pages through it without a 500, a lost row or a repeat, or excludes it deliberately and says so. GET /invoices/inv_a1_6, which already answers 500 because InvoiceOut requires issued_at, answers 200 with issued_at null. docs/api.md gains the endpoint with its sort key and where never-issued invoices fall, and its Money section, which wrongly describes decimal strings, is corrected to integer minor units. Any index goes in a new migration file that survives a re-run, never an edit to a released one. Tests cover the cases above and make check (ruff and pytest) passes. Nothing is committed.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository (ruff check and pytest), and it runs new tests that call the new invoice list endpoint, beyond the 13 tests in the fixture

A GET endpoint lists one customer's invoices (for example /customers/{customer_id}/invoices, or /invoices?customer_id=...), requires the Bearer API key like the other routes, answers the same page shape as GET /customers ({"items": [...], "next_cursor": ... or null}), and each item carries money as integers in minor units with the currency, as GET /invoices/{invoice_id} returns through InvoiceOut

Asking for another organisation's customer (for example key-org-b asking for cus_a1) or for a customer id that does not exist answers 404 with the not_found error envelope, not 200 with an empty list, and a test proves the cross-organisation case

Drafts are never returned or requestable: the unfiltered list for cus_a1 does not contain inv_a1_5, status=draft is a 422 or returns no invoice, an unknown status (for example status=bogus) is a 422 in the validation_failed envelope, and tests cover the draft exclusion and a rejected status value

inv_a1_6 (a void invoice of cus_a1 that was never issued, issued_at NULL, which docs/adr/0002 says is visible) does not break the list: GET of cus_a1's invoices with no filter and with status=void answers 200, never 500. Either inv_a1_6 is returned exactly once when paging with limit=1 through every page (placed by a stated rule such as created_at as the fallback, or last), or the run excludes it deliberately and its final message names that exclusion and why. A test covers this row

GET /invoices/inv_a1_6 answers 200 with issued_at null in the output repository (in the fixture it answers 500, because InvoiceOut declares issued_at as a required string and the list items share that shape), no draft becomes readable through that change, and a test covers it

Paging with limit=1 through every page of cus_a1's unfiltered list returns every invoice the endpoint lists exactly once, with no repeat and no gap, including across the tie between inv_a1_2 and inv_a1_3 (they share both issued_at 2026-07-01T09:00:00Z and created_at 2026-06-28T10:00:00Z, so the tie exists whichever of those the run sorts by): the ORDER BY and the cursor comparison use the same key with id as the tie-break, and a test pages across that tie

The status value reaches SQL only as a bound parameter (a `?` placeholder or a fixed mapping to literal SQL), never interpolated into the SQL string, and the run adds no `# noqa` for S608 or any other rule

Paging works with the status filter and within its bounds: with status=void and limit=1, following next_cursor returns inv_a1_3 and inv_a1_6 each exactly once, nothing else, and ends with next_cursor null (or, if the run deliberately excludes inv_a1_6 as allowed above, returns inv_a1_3 alone); limit defaults to 20, limit=101 is a 422 and a malformed cursor is a 422 (reusing the helpers in app/pagination.py, or equivalent behaviour)

The new SQL lives in a repository module and runs through the async methods of app.db.Database (no route or service opens sqlite3 or blocks the event loop, docs/adr/0001); the filter, the cursor comparison and LIMIT are applied in SQL, not by loading all of the customer's invoices and slicing them in Python; the route declares its response model and returns Pydantic models, not raw dicts or sqlite3 rows

The Money section of docs/api.md is corrected in the output repository to describe what the API returns (integer minor units such as amount_minor with the currency), instead of the decimal strings it described; noting the contradiction only in the final message does not pass

docs/api.md in the output repository lists the new endpoint and states what "newest first" sorts by for it (issued_at, created_at, or a fallback between them) and where an invoice that was never issued appears in that order (or that it is excluded); the final message names the same choice. Listing the path in the endpoints table alone does not pass

Migrations 0001 to 0003 under migrations/ are byte-for-byte unchanged; if the run adds an index for the new query it is a new file such as migrations/0004_*.sql whose statements can be run a second time without failing (for example CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS), since app/migrate.py records a file only after executescript has committed it; if it adds none, the final message says whether the query needs one

No existing route changes behaviour for the rows it already served and no existing test is deleted or weakened; the fixture's tests in tests/test_customers.py, tests/test_invoices.py and tests/test_webhooks.py still pass unchanged or with only additions; pyproject.toml gains no dependency and no ruff rule is disabled
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit on feature/INV-41-customer-invoices and the changes are left in the working tree

The final message says which checks were run and their result, and states whether any new migration was applied to a persistent database (for example a developer's invoices.db or any database the run did not create itself); applying it to the tests' temporary databases or to a throwaway scratch database the run created and names (for example to read EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN) counts as not applied, provided the message says so rather than implying a real database was migrated
If the run records a decision anywhere in the repository, it is not marked Accepted or approved and names no decider (a person, role or team) who did not make the decision in this conversation
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: refund-webhook-review
evals.prompt: Can you review feature/refund-webhook before I merge it into main? Refunds from the payment provider need to show up on invoices. Don't change anything, just tell me what's wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: A findings-first review of the one commit on feature/refund-webhook against main, with file and line or function for each finding, ranked by severity and a clear not-ready-to-merge verdict. The findings a senior reviewer must catch: the provider posts every event to the one configured URL (docs/provider-webhooks.md), so the new /webhooks/refunds route never receives refunds while /webhooks/payments answers 200 "ignored" and the provider never retries; the provider's refund amount_minor is the running total refunded, not a delta, so adding it double counts partial refunds and the branch's partial-refund test encodes the wrong model; the empty default secret plus the `if not secret: return True` bypass, which also leaves /webhooks/payments verifiable with an empty key; the signature is computed over re-serialised JSON instead of the raw body, after the body is parsed and logged; malformed or invalid bodies answer 500 instead of 401 or 422; no processed_events dedupe despite at-least-once delivery; f-string SQL with its lint silenced by noqa; time.sleep on the event loop in a retry that catches every OperationalError and can outlast the provider's 10 second deadline; the full payload with customer_email logged; an unowned create_task; no validation of the refund amount, the invoice's status or the event type; tests that cover none of the failure cases. Every claim is true of the code (httpx has a 5 s default timeout; the tests and ruff pass). The review changes nothing in the repository and states whether make check was run.
expectations: The repository is unchanged (git status --porcelain is empty, no tracked file edited, no file added outside what .gitignore ignores, no commit, feature/refund-webhook still checked out at the fixture commit; caches that running make check leaves, such as .ruff_cache/, __pycache__/ or .pytest_cache/, do not count as changes) and the review gives a clear verdict that the branch is not ready to merge as it is

The review says that the provider posts every event type to the one URL configured for the account (docs/provider-webhooks.md), so the new POST /webhooks/refunds route receives nothing in production, while refund.succeeded events that reach /webhooks/payments are answered 200 with status "ignored" and therefore never retried: refunds are silently lost

The review flags that docs/provider-webhooks.md defines a refund event's data.amount_minor as the total refunded so far, not this refund's amount, so `amount_refunded_minor + amount` double counts every partial refund after the first (10000 then 15000 records 25000), that tests/test_refunds.py::test_partial_refunds_add_up asserts the wrong model, and that the update should set the running total (ideally never lowering it, since refund events can arrive out of order) rather than add to it

The review flags the unsafe secret default: app/config.py changes webhook_secret from a required SecretStr to `str = ""`, and check_signature in app/webhooks/refunds.py returns True when the secret is empty, so a deployment without INVOICES_WEBHOOK_SECRET accepts forged refund events instead of failing at startup; and it notes that the same change also weakens POST /webhooks/payments (an empty HMAC key anyone can use, or settings that no longer fail fast for every endpoint relying on the secret)

The review flags that the refund signature is checked over json.dumps(await request.json()) rather than the raw request body, so genuine provider signatures (computed over the bytes as sent) will not match, that tests/test_refunds.py passes only because it signs compact json.dumps output, and that app/webhooks/signing.py already has a correct verify_signature (raw body, hmac.compare_digest) the branch should reuse or that the new `==` comparison is not constant time

The review flags the order of work in refund_webhook: the body is parsed (request.json() and RefundEvent.model_validate) and logged before the signature is checked, so unauthenticated input is processed first; the check must come first, over the raw bytes

The review flags that a request whose body is not JSON or is missing a field answers 500 (JSONDecodeError or pydantic ValidationError, neither mapped to the error envelope) instead of a 4xx such as 401 or 422; naming the consequence (the provider retries a 5xx for up to 3 days) is welcome but not required

The review flags that refund events are not recorded in processed_events, so a redelivered event (delivery is at least once per docs/provider-webhooks.md and migrations/0003_processed_events.sql) is applied a second time, unlike apply_payment in app/webhooks/service.py

The review flags the SQL in apply_refund built with an f-string from payload values (injection through invoice_id), and that the `# noqa: S608` on that line silences the ruff rule that would have caught it
The review flags that _wait calls time.sleep and is called from the async apply_refund, blocking the event loop for every request during retries (contrary to docs/adr/0001)

The review flags that the retry loop in apply_refund catches every sqlite3.OperationalError (a missing column or bad SQL is retried like a lock) and that its worst case, three attempts each waiting up to the 5 s busy timeout of Database.connect plus about 1.4 s of sleeps, is roughly 16 s, beyond the provider's 10 second answer deadline, so the provider times out and redelivers an event whose first attempt may still commit

The review flags that log.info in refund_webhook logs the whole payload, which includes data.customer_email, personal data that docs/provider-webhooks.md says never to log, and that it does so before the signature is checked (anyone can write to the log)
The review flags the asyncio.create_task(notify_accounts(...)) whose task nobody keeps or awaits: it can be garbage collected mid-flight and its failures are lost

The review flags at least two missing checks on the refund itself, from: amount_minor may be zero or negative (RefundData has no gt=0 constraint, unlike EventData); the refund is not limited to the amount paid; the currency is not compared with the invoice's; the update has no status condition, so a refund lands on a draft or void invoice (docs/adr/0002); the route never checks event.type; the update's matched row count is ignored, so an unknown invoice id still answers applied

The review says the branch's tests miss the failure cases and names all three of these gaps, in any wording or place: no test sends a bad or missing signature, none redelivers an event, and none sends a body with the provider's own spacing (bytes that differ from compact json.dumps) to /webhooks/refunds
Each finding names the file and the line or function it is about, and the findings are ordered or labelled by severity

Every defect the review reports is real when checked against the code; in particular it does not claim that the tests or make check fail on the branch (ruff and all 15 tests pass there), and it does not say the notify call has no timeout (httpx.AsyncClient applies a 5 s default per phase; saying 5 s is too long, or that the call should not run from the request at all, is fine)
The review states whether it ran make check or the tests, and reports the result it saw; if it did not run them it says so
